description:
Slow tests are refactored, never excused. 0b35be66's final whole-workspace run flagged one more unit test over the 2 s limit, which f487aeef would turn into a failing cargo-ci.

## Background

The limits are the per-layer values in `dev/benchmarks/per-test-durations-1eb949a5/README.md`: 2 s for lib and bin targets, 6 s for `crates/*/tests/*` targets. In 0b35be66's run `after2` (2026-11-08 02:07, 1-minute load 2.13), `commands::bootstrap::tests::test_open_repository_replays_original_audit_before_recovered_write_policy` took 3.443 s; earlier runs measured 1.79 s and 1.84 s. The method and evidence format are in `dev/benchmarks/per-test-durations-1eb949a5/remeasure-0b35be66/README.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The test runs under the 2 s unit limit in a whole-workspace nextest run on a quiet host (1-minute load below 4), and a committed note under `dev/benchmarks/per-test-durations-1eb949a5/` records its measured duration before and after with the run's load.
- [hard] REQ-02: The refactored test does not sleep or wait on wall-clock time to observe the property it owns.
- [hard] REQ-03: The test still owns the property it owned before, at the same or a cheaper layer, with no weakened assertion, no ignored test and no deletion without the property moving to another owning test.

## Notes

If the test cannot meet the limit without losing its property, report it as a blocking concern rather than raising the limit.
title: Bring the bootstrap audit-replay test under the unit limit
